title: Coconut Farm: Division
seo_title: Division Class 5 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 9)
standard_code: Class 5, Maths Mela Chapter 9: Coconut Farm
standard_text: Division: dividing larger numbers by 1- and 2-digit numbers, remainders, and solving problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 5)
meta_desc: Class 5 Coconut Farm worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 9): short division, remainders and division stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Divide each place from the left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Short division: 864 ÷ 4 → 8 ÷ 4 = 2, 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2, 24 ÷ 4 = 6, so 216.
  • Think about the remainder: 50 coconuts in bags of 8 needs 7 bags.

Examples

Example

1,236 coconuts are packed 6 to a sack.

1,236 ÷ 6

Answer: 206 sacks

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Skipping a zero in the answerWrite 0 when a place cannot be divided.
Ignoring what the remainder meansSometimes you need one more group.

faq.a: A quick written method for dividing by a 1-digit number.

faq.q: What do I do with a remainder?
faq.a: It depends on the story: round up, round down or share it.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Answer: 16. Check: 16 × 3 = 48.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Answer: 29. Check: 29 × 3 = 87.

items.q: Use short division to work out 68 ÷ 4.
items.e: 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Answer: 17. Check: 17 × 4 = 68.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Answer: 14. Check: 14 × 6 = 84.

items.q: Use short division to work out 679 ÷ 7.
items.e: 7 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 67; 67 ÷ 7 = 9 r 4, carry the 4 to make 49; 49 ÷ 7 = 7. Answer: 97. Check: 97 × 7 = 679.

items.q: Tara uses short division for 724 ÷ 4. First, 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. What does she divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 hundreds, which is 30 tens. Write it as a small 3 in front of the 2, so you divide 32 next: 32 ÷ 4 = 8. The whole answer: 181.

items.q: Use short division to work out 532 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 4 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Answer: 133. Check: 133 × 4 = 532.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 4 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 4 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Answer: 168. Check: 168 × 4 = 672.

items.q: Use short division to work out 804 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 3 = 6 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Answer: 268. Check: 268 × 3 = 804.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 7, so carry the 7 to make 71; 71 ÷ 8 = 8 r 7, carry the 7 to make 72; 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Answer: 89. Check: 89 × 8 = 712.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 6 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer: 156. Check: 156 × 6 = 936.

items.q: Use short division to work out 98 ÷ 7.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Answer: 14. Check: 14 × 7 = 98.

items.q: Kabir works out 438 ÷ 3 = 112 r 2. What mistake did he make?
c: He divided by the wrong number
He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Kabir divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 3 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Answer: 146. Check: 146 × 3 = 438.

items.q: Arjun uses short division for 811 ÷ 6. First, 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. What does he divide next?
items.e: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. The remainder 2 is 2 hundreds, which is 20 tens. Write it as a small 2 in front of the 1, so you divide 21 next: 21 ÷ 6 = 3 r 3. The whole answer: 135 r 1.

items.q: Harsh uses short division for 721 ÷ 3. First, 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1. What does he divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 2, so you divide 12 next: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. The whole answer: 240 r 1.

items.q: Use short division to work out 942 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4, carry the 4 to make 42; 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Answer: 157. Check: 157 × 6 = 942.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 8 = 1; 8 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 8 = 2. Answer: 102. Check: 102 × 8 = 816.

items.q: Simran works out 387 ÷ 3 = 122 r 1. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not carry the remainders
She divided by the wrong number
She missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Simran divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 3 ÷ 3 = 1; 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Answer: 129. Check: 129 × 3 = 387.

items.q: 984 ÷ 4 = 246. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 246 × 4 = 984, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: 924 ÷ 7 = 132. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 132 × 7 = 924, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 3 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 3 = 3 r 2. Answer: 243 r 2. Check: 243 × 3 + 2 = 731.

items.q: Use short division to work out 344 ÷ 5.
items.e: 5 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 5 = 6 r 4, carry the 4 to make 44; 44 ÷ 5 = 8 r 4. Answer: 68 r 4. Check: 68 × 5 + 4 = 344.

items.q: Use short division to work out 817 ÷ 5.
items.e: 8 ÷ 5 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 5 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 5 = 3 r 2. Answer: 163 r 2. Check: 163 × 5 + 2 = 817.

items.q: You divide a number by 4. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 1 to 3 (or 0). If you have 4 or more left, 4 goes in again.

items.q: Use short division to work out 825 ÷ 7.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 7 = 1 r 5, carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 7 = 7 r 6. Answer: 117 r 6. Check: 117 × 7 + 6 = 825.

items.q: Use short division to work out 534 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 4 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 4 = 3 r 2. Answer: 133 r 2. Check: 133 × 4 + 2 = 534.

items.q: Use short division to work out 857 ÷ 7.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 7 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 7 = 2 r 3. Answer: 122 r 3. Check: 122 × 7 + 3 = 857.

items.q: Use short division to work out 736 ÷ 3.
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 3 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 3 = 5 r 1. Answer: 245 r 1. Check: 245 × 3 + 1 = 736.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 6 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 6 = 8 r 4. Answer: 128 r 4. Check: 128 × 6 + 4 = 772.

items.q: Use short division to work out 881 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 3 = 9 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 3 = 3 r 2. Answer: 293 r 2. Check: 293 × 3 + 2 = 881.

items.q: Riya works out 288 ÷ 5 = 56 r 8. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the quotient
She did not carry the remainders
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 8 is more than 5, so 5 goes in once more: 8 − 5 = 3. The answer is 57 r 3. Check: 57 × 5 + 3 = 288.

items.q: Work out 76 ÷ 8. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: 76 ÷ 8 = 9 r 4. The remainder 4 out of 8 is 48. Simplify: divide the numerator and the denominator by 4 to get 12. Answer: 9 12.

items.q: Work out 64 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 64 ÷ 5 = 12 r 4. The remainder 4 out of 5 is 45 = 0.8. So the answer is 12.8, not 12.4.

items.q: Work out 79 ÷ 6. Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 79 ÷ 6 = 13 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 6, so it is 16. Answer: 13 16.

items.q: Work out 953 ÷ 3. Give the remainder as a whole number.
Work out 77 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 77 ÷ 4 = 19 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 4, so it is 14. Answer: 19 14.

items.q: Work out 54 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 54 ÷ 4 = 13 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 4 is 24 = 0.5. So the answer is 13.5, not 13.2.

items.q: Work out 41 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 41 ÷ 5 = 8 r 1. The remainder 1 out of 5 is 15 = 0.2. So the answer is 8.2, not 8.1.

items.q: Work out 35 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3. The remainder 3 out of 4 is 34 = 0.75. So the answer is 8.75, not 8.3.

items.q: Work out 57 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 57 ÷ 5 = 11 r 2. The remainder 2 is 2 out of 5, so it is 25. Answer: 11 25.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 5,612 ÷ 7?
items.e: 5,612 is close to 5,600, and 56 ÷ 7 = 8, so 5,600 ÷ 7 = 800. The exact answer is 801 r 5.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 4 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 4 = 6 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Answer: 1,366. Check: 1,366 × 4 = 5,464.

items.q: Ayaan works out 8,008 ÷ 4 = 22. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the answer
He did not carry the remainders
items.e: Check: 22 × 4 = 88, not 8,008. When 4 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer. 8 ÷ 4 = 2; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Answer: 2,002. Check: 2,002 × 4 = 8,008.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 3 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 3 = 9 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Answer: 1,399. Check: 1,399 × 3 = 4,197.

items.q: Use short division to work out 5,976 ÷ 9.
items.e: 9 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 9 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 57; 57 ÷ 9 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Answer: 664. Check: 664 × 9 = 5,976.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 7 = 2; 7 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Answer: 204. Check: 204 × 7 = 1,428.

items.q: Use short division to work out 6,232 ÷ 6.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 6 = 3 r 5, carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 6 = 8 r 4. Answer: 1,038 r 4. Check: 1,038 × 6 + 4 = 6,232.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 5, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 6 = 9 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Answer: 1,099. Check: 1,099 × 6 = 6,594.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 3 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 3 = 7; 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Answer: 714. Check: 714 × 3 = 2,142.

items.q: Use short division to work out 2,736 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 4 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 4 = 8 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 684. Check: 684 × 4 = 2,736.

items.q: Use short division to work out 9,678 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6; 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Answer: 1,613. Check: 1,613 × 6 = 9,678.

items.q: How many digits will the quotient of 5,227 ÷ 6 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 5 is less than 6, so there are no thousands. The quotient starts in the hundreds place. 5,227 ÷ 6 = 871 r 1.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 58; 58 ÷ 8 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 8 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 8 = 4 r 1. Answer: 734 r 1. Check: 734 × 8 + 1 = 5,873.

items.q: Varun works out 8,036 ÷ 4 = 29. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the quotient
He did not carry the remainders
items.e: Check: 29 × 4 = 116, not 8,036. When 4 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient. 8 ÷ 4 = 2; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 4 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Answer: 2,009. Check: 2,009 × 4 = 8,036.

items.q: Dev works out 1,505 ÷ 5 = 31. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the quotient
items.e: Check: 31 × 5 = 155, not 1,505. When 5 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the quotient. 5 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 5 = 3; 5 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Answer: 301. Check: 301 × 5 = 1,505.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 56; 56 ÷ 7 = 8; 7 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 7 = 2. Answer: 802. Check: 802 × 7 = 5,614.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 6 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer: 1,036. Check: 1,036 × 6 = 6,216.

items.q: Use short division to work out 4,016 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the quotient; 4 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 1,004. Check: 1,004 × 4 = 4,016.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4,905 ÷ 7?
items.e: 4,905 is close to 4,900, and 49 ÷ 7 = 7, so 4,900 ÷ 7 = 700. The exact answer is 700 r 5.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 3 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 3 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Answer: 2,746. Check: 2,746 × 3 = 8,238.

items.q: A 55 m rope is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 55 ÷ 4 = 13 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. So the answer is 13 34 m.

items.q: 4 friends share 27 pizzas equally. How much pizza does each friend get? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 27 ÷ 4 = 6 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. So the answer is 6 34 pizzas.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 7 = 164 r 3
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 164 × 7 = 1,148 and 1,148 + 3 = 1,151. Check: 1,151 ÷ 7 = 164 r 3.

items.q: 152 ÷ 8 = 19. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 19 × 8 = 152, which matches.

items.q: 209 people want a boat ride on the lake. Each boat trip takes 9 people. 209 ÷ 9 = 23 r 2. How many boat trips are needed?
items.e: 23 trips hold 23 × 9 = 207 people. 2 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 24 trips. Round up.

items.q: 335 ÷ 8 = 41 r 7. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor, then add the remainder: 41 × 8 = 328 and 328 + 7 = 335.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 9 = 28 r 7
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 28 × 9 = 252 and 252 + 7 = 259. Check: 259 ÷ 9 = 28 r 7.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 6 = 101 r 2
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 101 × 6 = 606 and 606 + 2 = 608. Check: 608 ÷ 6 = 101 r 2.

items.q: 129 ÷ 9 = 14 r 3. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor, then add the remainder: 14 × 9 = 126 and 126 + 3 = 129.

items.q: A baker has 70 cupcakes. Each box holds 6 cupcakes. 70 ÷ 6 = 11 r 4. How many boxes can the baker fill?
items.e: 70 ÷ 6 = 11 r 4. The 4 cupcakes left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 11 boxes.

items.q: 194 students are going on a school excursion. Each minibus has 9 seats for students. Ananya works out 194 ÷ 9 = 21 r 5 and says 21 minibuses are needed. What is the right answer?
items.e: 21 minibuses only seat 21 × 9 = 189 students. The other 5 students still need seats, so Ananya rounded the wrong way. Round up: 22 minibuses.

items.q: A 38 m rope is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 38 ÷ 4 = 9 r 2. Rope can be cut into parts, so share the 2 m left over: 24 = 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5. Each piece is 9.5 m, not 9.2 m.

items.q: A shop has 99 batteries. It sells them in packs of 4. How many full packs can the shop make?
items.e: 99 ÷ 4 = 24 r 3. The 3 batteries left over are not enough to make another pack, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 24 packs.

items.q: 227 Class 5 students are going on school camp. Each tent sleeps 6 students. How many tents are needed?
items.e: 227 ÷ 6 = 37 r 5. 37 tents hold 37 × 6 = 222 students. 5 students still need a place, so you need 1 more: 38 tents. Round up.

items.q: A bakery has 171 lamingtons. Each box holds 6 lamingtons. How many boxes can be filled?
items.e: 171 ÷ 6 = 28 r 3. The 3 lamingtons left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 28 boxes.

items.q: A teacher shares 184 stickers equally between 6 groups. Each group gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: 184 ÷ 6 = 30 r 4. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 4 stickers.

items.q: 43 guests are coming to the school trivia night. Each table seats 8 guests. How many tables are needed?
items.e: 43 ÷ 8 = 5 r 3. 5 tables hold 5 × 8 = 40 guests. 3 guests still need a place, so you need 1 more: 6 tables. Round up.

items.q: A teacher needs 213 glue sticks for the term. Glue sticks come in packs of 6. How many packs must she buy?
items.e: 213 ÷ 6 = 35 r 3. 35 packs give 35 × 6 = 210 glue sticks. She still needs 3 glue sticks more, so she must buy 1 more pack: 36 packs. Round up.

items.q: The school library has 473 new books. Each shelf holds 9 books. How many shelves can be filled completely?
items.e: 473 ÷ 9 = 52 r 5. The 5 books left over are not enough to fill another shelf, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 52 shelves.

items.q: 32 cakes are shared equally between 3 classes for an end-of-term party. How much cake does each class get? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 32 ÷ 3 = 10 r 2. The 2 left-over cakes can be cut and shared too: 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Each class gets 10 23 cakes.

items.q: 39 pizzas are shared equally between 4 tables at a party. How much pizza does each table get?
items.e: Divide: 39 ÷ 4 = 9 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. Each gets 9 34 pizzas.

items.q: A farm collects 1,907 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 6 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 6 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 47; 47 ÷ 6 = 7 r 5. So 1,907 ÷ 6 = 317 r 5. 317 boxes are not enough: 5 eggs would still need a box. You need 1 more, so the answer is 318 boxes.

items.q: A garden centre has 1,523 bulbs. It packs them in bags of 6 and fills as many bags as it can. How many bulbs are not in a bag?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 6 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 6 = 5 r 2, carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 6 = 3 r 5. So 1,523 ÷ 6 = 253 r 5. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 5 bulbs.

items.q: Dev is putting 354 photos into an album. Each page holds 4 photos. How many pages does he need?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2. So 354 ÷ 4 = 88 r 2. 88 pages are not enough: 2 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so the answer is 89 pages.

items.q: 274 playing cards are dealt out equally to 6 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 6 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4. So 274 ÷ 6 = 45 r 4. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 cards.

items.q: Tara bakes 35 flapjacks. She shares them equally between 4 friends. How many flapjacks does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. Each gets 8 34 flapjacks.

items.q: 339 people are coming to a school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 8. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 8 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3. So 339 ÷ 8 = 42 r 3. 42 rows are not enough: 3 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 43 rows.

items.q: Rehan shares 191 sweets equally into 9 party bags. Each bag gets as many as possible. How many sweets are left over?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 9 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 9 = 1 r 2. So 191 ÷ 9 = 21 r 2. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 2 sweets.

items.q: Aditi is making necklaces. Each necklace needs 9 beads. She has 212 beads. How many necklaces can she make?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 9 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 9 = 3 r 5. So 212 ÷ 9 = 23 r 5. The 5 beads left over are not enough to make another necklace, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 23 necklaces.

items.q: A farm has 1,983 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 6 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 6 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the answer and the remainder is 3. So 1,983 ÷ 6 = 330 r 3. The 3 eggs left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 330 boxes.

items.q: A nursery has 1,388 seedlings. It plants them in trays of 6 and fills as many trays as it can. How many seedlings are not in a tray?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 6 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. So 1,388 ÷ 6 = 231 r 2. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 2 seedlings.

items.q: Diya runs 1,494 m by running 6 laps of the school oval. Each lap is the same length. How long is one lap?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 6 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 6 = 4 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. So 1,494 ÷ 6 = 249. There is no remainder, so the answer is 249 m. Check: 249 × 6 = 1,494.

items.q: A farm collects 1,797 eggs. It packs them in cartons of 6. How many cartons does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 6 = 2 r 5, carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 6 = 9 r 5, carry the 5 to make 57; 57 ÷ 6 = 9 r 3. So 1,797 ÷ 6 = 299 r 3. 299 cartons are not enough: 3 eggs would still need a carton. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 300 cartons.

items.q: 268 people are coming to the school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 9. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 9 = 2 r 8, carry the 8 to make 88; 88 ÷ 9 = 9 r 7. So 268 ÷ 9 = 29 r 7. 29 rows are not enough: 7 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 30 rows.

items.q: A school orders 2,832 exercise books. They come in packs of 8. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 8 = 3 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 8 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 8 = 4. So 2,832 ÷ 8 = 354. There is no remainder, so the answer is 354 packs. Check: 354 × 8 = 2,832.

items.q: A book has 376 pages. Zoya reads the same number of pages each day and finishes it in 4 days. How many pages does she read each day?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 37; 37 ÷ 4 = 9 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. So 376 ÷ 4 = 94. There is no remainder, so the answer is 94 pages. Check: 94 × 4 = 376.

items.q: A farm packs 1,355 mangoes into trays of 9. How many full trays can it pack?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 9 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 9 = 5; 9 does not go into 5, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 5. So 1,355 ÷ 9 = 150 r 5. The 5 mangoes left over are not enough to fill another tray, so round down. The answer is 150 trays.

items.q: Gauri is putting 355 photos into an album. Each page holds 4 photos. How many pages does she need?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3. So 355 ÷ 4 = 88 r 3. 88 pages are not enough: 3 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 89 pages.

items.q: Ishaan deals 159 playing cards equally to 6 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 6 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3. So 159 ÷ 6 = 26 r 3. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 3 cards.

items.q: 188 students are going to the athletics carnival. Each minibus has 9 seats for students. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 9 = 2; 9 does not go into 8, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 8. So 188 ÷ 9 = 20 r 8. 20 minibuses are not enough: 8 students would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 21 minibuses.
